blocks.text: Compose Watch syncs host changes into the running container (or rebuilds it) according to rules; a bind mount shares the host directory live in both directions.
$ docker compose watch      # or: docker compose up --watch

rows: Files written by the container user

items: Sync writes to the writable layer: recreate discards it, and the next watch resyncs.
`--reload` still does the restarting; Watch only delivers files.
Combine them: bind-mount `migrations/`, watch-sync the source.

blocks.text: Q: "Bind mount or Compose Watch for dev?" A: "Watch when bind mounts are slow or cause permission problems, or when dependency changes should trigger rebuilds; bind mounts when tools in the container must write back to the repo, such as Alembic autogenerate or formatters."

items: Binds for files generated in the container.
